1 Description of Planned Activities
In accordance with the requirements of Title 10 of the Code of Federal Regulations (10 CFR)
50.10, “License required; limited work authorization,” SMR, LLC, on behalf of Palisades SMR,
LLC, hereby submits the enclosed application requesting the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory
Commission (NRC) review and approval of a limited work authorization (LWA) to begin
construction of a dual-unit SMR-300 plant located at the Palisades Energy Center (PEC) in
Covert, Michigan. The units are individually named Pioneer Unit 1 and Pioneer Unit 2.
This submittal is the first part (Part 1) of a construction permit application for a utilization facility
under 10 CFR Part 50 to authorize the construction of a dual-unit SMR-300 plant, consisting of
two SMR-300 individual small modular reactors. This Part 1 includes a request for an LWA, an
exemption from 10 CFR 50.10(d) to authorize certain construction activities prior to issuance of
a full construction permit, an exemption from 10 CFR 50.10(c) to allow permanent installation of
retaining walls, and an exemption from 10 CFR 50.33(f)(1) and 10 CFR Part 50 requirements to
identify specific sources of funding at this stage of the project. Part 2 will include the remaining
information to support issuance of the construction permit and will be filed no later than
18 months after this Part 1 submittal.
Holtec is performing non-construction activities, as defined by 10 CFR 50.10(a) and Holtec
plans to perform additional non-construction activities prior to LWA approval. These activities are
described in Section 1.1.
Holtec requests an exemption to allow installation of permanent support of excavation (SOE)
walls (a construction activity) prior to LWA approval. The exemption request is included in
Enclosure IV of this application. The activities addressed by this exemption request are
described in Section 1.2.
Holtec requests approval to perform construction activities under the LWA, consistent with
10 CFR 50.10(d). In addition, Holtec requests an exemption to allow construction activities
beyond those permitted by 10 CFR 50.10(d). The exemption request is included in Enclosure IV
of this application. The construction activities are described in Section 1.3.
Descriptions of the Pioneer Units 1 and 2 structures, systems, and components (SSCs) to be
installed are provided in the preliminary safety analysis report (PSAR) included as Enclosure II
of this application.

1.1 Non-Construction Activities
Site characterization and other non-construction activities have been ongoing at PEC since
2024. A permitting plan, including applicable environmental and construction permits, has been
established and implemented to acquire appropriate local, state, and federal permits.
Site preparation activities will include demolition of current structures, clearing and grading of
the site, paving access roads and parking lots, and establishment of access control. Holtec will
establish drainage, erosion control, and stormwater management. Construction support will
commence, including installation of temporary power, fuel storage tanks, a concrete batch plant,
and structural module fabrication areas.
Excavation and the installation of certain non-safety-related SSCs that do not meet the definition
of a construction activity in 10 CFR 50.10(d) will be installed. These activities may commence

prior to or after approval of this LWA application, and the activities will continue during the LWA
construction period.
Non-construction activities will include:
   •   Install buried piping for the Raw Water System (RWS), Circulating Water System (CRS),
       and Service Water System (SWS).
   •   Install associated basins and cooling towers for the CRS and SWS.
   •   Install intake and outfall structures in Lake Michigan.
   •   Fabricate but not install modules for the SMR-300 major structures.
   •   Establish the Turbine Building (TB) foundation and install the turbine pedestal.

1.2 Installation of Permanent Support of Excavation Walls
Permanent SOE walls will be used for the major structures, including the unitized Containment
Structures (CSs), the shared Reactor Auxiliary Building (RAB), the unitized Intermediate
Buildings (IBs) and the unitized TBs. An exemption request is included in Enclosure IV of this
application to request approval to allow installation of the permanent SOE walls prior to
issuance of the LWA.

1.3 LWA Construction Activities
After approval of the LWA, Holtec will perform soil improvement to enhance the physical and
mechanical properties of the soil within the excavation and install foundations for CSs (one for
each unit), the RAB (shared between the two units) and for the IBs (one for each unit). A single
basemat supports both CSs and a portion of the shared RAB (the portion that is “plant south,”
referred to as the RAB-S). The remainder of the RAB (RAB-N) is supported by a separate
basemat at a shallower elevation.
An exemption request is included in Enclosure IV of this application to allow additional
construction activities under the LWA.
The additional construction activities for each unit include installation of the following:
       •   Steel-concrete containment vessel (SCCV) from the foundation to plant grade level
       •   Interior, below-grade structures of the SCCV, specifically:
               o Bio-shield wall
               o Passive core makeup water tank walls
               o Spent fuel pool walls
               o Walls surrounding the reactor pressure vessel cavity
               o Steam generator support block
               o Walls surrounding steam generator support block
               o Walls surrounding the Chemical and Volume Control System regenerative
                    heat exchanger
               o Elevator shaft walls
               o Reactor coolant pump support blocks
       •   Transfer girder.
       •   Structural steel for the TB.
       •   CRS pumps and valves.
       •   Below-grade IB walls.

2 General and Financial Information
2.1 General Information
This construction permit application (CPA) is being submitted by SMR, LLC on behalf of
Palisades SMR, LLC, a wholly-owned subsidiary of Holtec International, for the construction of a
dual-unit SMR-300 plant located at the Palisades Energy Center (PEC) in Covert, Michigan.
2.1.1 Description of Applicant
Palisades SMR, LLC is a special purpose entity formed to support development and financing of
the Project and to serve as the NRC-licensed owner. Palisades SMR, LLC is a direct, wholly
owned subsidiary of Nuclear Asset Management Company, LLC (NAMCO). NAMCO is a direct,
wholly owned subsidiary of Holtec Power, Inc. Holtec Power is a direct, wholly owned subsidiary
of Holtec International. Figure 2-1 provides an organizational chart with the applicable
organizational structure of the owning and operating entities for Pioneer Units 1 and 2.
                             Figure 2-1 Corporate Organization




Holtec International is a Delaware corporation and the ultimate parent company of all the
relevant entities who will own and operate the Project. Holtec International developed the SMR-
300vdesign and will provide corporate and financial support for the project, but the applicant and
the entity directly responsible for licensing, and construction of the Project and for the conduct of
activities under the construction permit is Palisades SMR, LLC. SMR, LLC is providing licensing
support services, including pre-submittal engagement, submission of topical reports, and
development this application; however, SMR, LLC’s role in the Project is solely a support role as
a affiliated service company to Palisades SMR, LLC. SMR, LLC is not an applicant and is not
intended to be a license holder with direct responsibility for the conduct of activities under the
LWA or construction permit.

Because Palisades SMR, LLC is a newly formed entity, the information required by
10 CFR 50.33(f)(4) is included herein. Palisades SMR, LLC is a Delaware limited liability
company whose sole member is NAMCO. As of the date of this CPA, Palisades SMR, LLC has
no liabilities and no assets. The real property on which the Project will be constructed is
currently owned by Holtec Palisades, LLC, the licensed owner of the Palisades Nuclear Plant.
Prior to commencement of nuclear construction, Holtec Palisades, LLC will ensure that
Palisades SMR, LLC has the appropriate rights with respect to the Project site. Such

commencement of nuclear construction, Holtec International will ensure that Palisades SMR,
LLC is appropriately capitalized to carry out the obligations of Palisades SMR, LLC during
construction (including satisfying contractual payment obligations or financing covenants). As
the applicant, oner, and license holder, Palisades SMR, LLC will have the staffing and other
organizational resources required to implement all required programs to carry out the
obligations under the LWA and construction permit.
Palisades SMR, LLC’s sole member, NAMCO, holds 100% of the membership interests in
Palisades SMR, LLC. Palisades SMR, LLC is governed by its sole member with delegated
authority to officers, all of whom are listed in Table 2-1. These individuals are ultimately
accountable to the Holtec International Executive Committee, the members of which are listed in
Table 2-1.
SMR, LLC is a Holtec service company formed to support licensing activities for SMR-300
projects, including pre-submittal engagement and the development and submittal of topical
reports and applications for this project and other potential projects. In this service company
support role, SMR, LLC will not have direct responsibility for design, construction,
commissioning, operation, or any other nuclear safety activities license under the LWA or
construction permit. The following corporate information is provided regarding SMR, LLC;
however, SMR, LLC is not an applicant and is not intended to be a licensee. SMR, LLC’s sole
member, Holtec, holds 100% of the membership interest in SMR, LLC. SMR, LLC is governed
by its sole member with delegated authority to officers, all of whom are listed in Table 2-1. These
individuals are ultimately accountable to the Holtec International Executive Committee, the

Holtec International and its subsidiaries are currently supplying funding, staffing, and support

Holtec is the ultimate parent company of all the entities described in Table 2-1. Holtec is a
privately held corporation. It is owned by its shareholders as follows: (1) The Great Banyan

2.1.2 License Type
This submittal is the first part (Part 1) of a construction permit application for a utilization facility
under 10 CFR Part 50 to authorize the construction of a dual-unit SMR-300 plant. This Part 1
includes a request for a limited work authorization (LWA), an exemption from 10 CFR 50.10(d)
to authorize certain construction activities prior to issuance of a full construction permit, an
exemption from 10 CFR 50.10(c) to allow permanent installation of retaining walls, and an
exemption from 10 CFR 50.33(f)(1) and 10 CFR Part 50 requirements to identify specific
sources of funding at this stage of the project. Pursuant to 10 CFR 2.101(a)(9), this Part 1
includes general corporate and financial information, an environmental report, applicable
portions of the preliminary safety analysis report (PSAR) for the activities described in Section
1.3 of Enclosure I of this application, and a redress plan for those activities. Part 2 will include
the remaining information to support issuance of the construction permit and will be filed no later
than 18 months after this Part 1 submittal. At the appropriate Project phase, Palisades SMR,
LLC will apply for an operating license and applicable license(s) governing the possession or
use of byproduct material, source material, or special nuclear material under 10 CFR Parts 30,
40, and 70, as applicable.
2.1.3 Construction Schedule
Palisades SMR, LLC requests that NRC establish a review schedule that supports issuance of
the LWA and exemption from 10 CFR 50.10(d) by December 31, 2026, to support
commencement of the limited construction activities described in Section 1.3 of Enclosure I of
this application in 2027.
Subject to Palisades SMR, LLC’s submittal of Part 2 of the application and NRC’s issuance of a
construction permit, Palisades SMR, LLC expects to begin full-scope nuclear construction in the
fourth quarter in 2028. Construction of both units is expected to be completed by the end of
2031.
2.1.4 Technical Qualifications
Holtec, which is led by Dr. Krishna Singh, is an integrated technologies enterprise providing
innovative solutions, equipment, and services to the global nuclear, solar, geothermal, and fossil
power generation sectors of the energy industry. Holtec brings a broad corporate resume of
accomplishments in nuclear projects in the U.S. and abroad, a substantial list of ongoing and
satisfactorily completed nuclear projects (including many turnkey projects), and a long safety
and quality record that demonstrates its commitment to nuclear safety and excellence.
As an industry leader in nuclear fuel management systems, Holtec has extensive experience in
providing safety-related services to operating commercial power plants, as well as in designing,
manufacturing, and installing safety-related equipment, and possesses in-house capabilities to
design, engineer, analyze, construct, and deploy the technologies to manage used nuclear fuel
discharged from nuclear reactors. Holtec holds several certificates of compliance for dry storage
systems and has decades of experience implementing those systems under NRC quality
assurance programs.
Holtec is the ultimate upstream parent company of the licensed owner and decommissioning
operator of four Part 50 commercial reactor sites that have permanently ceased power
operations and are in various states of decommissioning: Oyster Creek, Pilgrim, Indian Point,
and Big Rock Point. Holtec is also the upstream parent of the licensed owner and operator of

the Palisades Nuclear Plant, the large light water reactor adjacent to the Project. Through its
subsidiaries, Holtec personnel have overseen the first-of-a-kind restart of the Palisades Nuclear
Plant following its shutdown in 2022. NRC recently approved the technical qualifications of
Holtec’s subsidiary, Palisades Energy, LLC, to operate the Palisades Nuclear Plant upon the
resumption of full power operations. Palisades Energy has training programs accredited by the
National Nuclear Accrediting Board. Palisades Energy is expected to serve as the licensed
operator of the Project following its completion but will not have responsibility for the conduct of
activities under the LWA or construction permit.
Holtec has invested in and developed the SMR-300 design for over a decade. Holtec’s reactor
designs have received cost-share funding from DOE via the Advanced Reactor Demonstration
Program (ARDP). The SMR-300 is an advanced pressurized light water reactor designed to use
commonly available nuclear fuel assemblies and able to leverage existing fleet operating
experience. The design was developed to leverage Holtec’s existing manufacturing
infrastructure to support modular fabrication of key components. The SMR-300 design is
described in more detail in the PSAR.
Holtec has teamed with Hyundai Engineering and Construction Co., Ltd. (HDEC) to support
site-specific engineering and balance-of-plant design and to serve as general construction
contractor for the Project, through its domestic subsidiary, Hyundai America, Inc., HDEC is a
Korean engineering, procurement, and construction (EPC) firm and leading international nuclear
contractor. The company has constructed over a dozen nuclear plants in South Korea and
recently served as lead contractor for the four APR-1400 Barakah units in the United Arab
Emirates.
The Project’s supply-chain will include established nuclear industry vendors, including
Framatome for fuel design and supply, and Mitsubishi Electric Corporation for instrumentation
and control (I&C) platform integration.
2.1.5 Foreign Ownership, Control, or Domination
Holtec is a privately held corporation owned by domestic trust companies that are in turn
controlled by a U.S. citizen. It is led by its Chief Executive Officer, a U.S. citizen, and
management of the company is vested in the Holtec executive leadership team, including the
Executive Committee members listed in Table 2-1. All the members of the Holtec Executive
Committee are U.S. citizens. All the managers and principal officers of Palisades SMR, LLC and
the intermediate Holtec International subsidiaries are U.S. citizens. As such, Palisades SMR,
LLC will not be owned, controlled, or dominated by any foreign person.
2.1.6 Restricted Data and Classified National Security Information
In accordance with 10 CFR 50.37, “Agreement limiting access to Classified Information,”
Palisades SMR, LLC agrees that it will appropriately safeguard such information and will not
permit any individual to have access except as authorized under 10 CFR Part 25, “Access
Authorization” and/or 10 CFR Part 95, “Facility Security Clearance and Safeguarding of National
Security Information and Restrict Data.”

2.2 Financial Qualifications
10 CFR 50.33(f)(1) requires a construction permit application to include estimates of total
construction costs and related fuel cycle costs, and sufficient information to demonstrate that


Holtec International Copyrighted Material                           September 2026 – Revision 1
                                             Page 2-6
 General and Financial Information                                             Pioneer Units 1 & 2
Construction Permit Application, Part 1                          General and Financial Information

the applicant has reasonable assurance of obtaining the funds necessary to cover those costs.
10 CFR Part 50, Appendix C, requires newly-formed companies that are not rate-regulated
utilities (such as Palisades SMR, LLC) to specifically identify the source(s) of funds that will be
used to cover the costs of construction. The Commission has recognized the difficulty (if not
impossibility) of making this showing with a high degree of specificity at the early stage of a
project, particularly given that submission of the initial NRC application is often a prerequisite to
obtaining financing. Accordingly, in SRM-SECY-13-0124 (Reference 1), the Commission
directed staff to undertaking rulemaking to amend the requirements of Part 50 to more closely
track the showing required for Part 70 fuel cycle facilities, “that the applicant appears to be
financially qualified.” Following this direction to staff, the Commission approved an exemption
from these Part 50 requirements in connection with its issuance of the South Texas Project,
Units 3 and 4 combined licenses in 2015 (Reference 2). Staff developed a proposed rule and
regulatory basis document to address the issue for all Part 50 applicants (References 3 and 4).
In SRM-SECY-18-0026, the Commission directed staff to instead address this topic in Part 53
rulemaking, which is still in process (Reference 5). NRC published a proposed rule in
September 24, 2026, that would revise 10 CFR 50.33(f) to require only that the Staff determine
the applicant “appears to be financially qualified to cover estimated construction cost.”
(Reference 8).
The financial realities that motivated the Commission to address this topic a decade ago have
not changed. Accordingly, Enclosure IV of this application includes an exemption request from
the parts of 10 CFR 50.33(f)(1) and Part 50, Appendix C, that require Palisades SMR, LLC to
identify specific source(s) of funds in this initial application. Instead, Palisades SMR, LLC
requests that it be allowed to demonstrate its qualifications under the 10 CFR Part 70 standard,
“that the applicant appears to be financially qualified,” Which would be consistent with the
proposed rule.
The section that follows includes Palisades SMR, LLC’s Financial Capacity Plan consistent with
NRC staff’s guidance in Reference 4, the requirements of 10 CFR 70.23(a)(5), the exemption
granted to the South Texas Project owners in Reference 2, and the information provided more
recently by similarly-situated applicants who requested exemptions from these same Part 50
requirements for the same reasons (References 6 and 7).

mechanicals. HDEC is intended to lead construction activities and developed bid pricing for
construction scopes in support of the estimate using both local and U.S. nation-wide
construction companies. Supply chain estimates by both Holtec International and HDEC
developed the remaining costs of the production plant. Transmission and Distribution cost
estimates are based on analysis by Sargent & Lundy. Palisades SMR, LLC’s costs are
developed through direct benchmarking of U.S. utility led projects. Fuel costs were developed
using publicly available information from leading uranium suppliers and validated through
quotation with Framatome. Note that the costs in Table 2-2 are the full Project costs, not just

2.2.2 Financial Capacity Plan
Anticipated Financing Structure
The Project was recently selected to receive $400 million in cost-shared funding from DOE for
the Generation III+ small modular reactor award authorized by the Consolidated Appropriations
Act of 2024 (PL 118-42). Subject to finalization of the award agreement, these funds are
expected to support certain engineering, licensing, procurement, and pre-construction activities.
The DOE award will reduce near-term private capital requirements for the Project and, together
with Holtec’s ongoing private investment, will support Project funding and continued schedule
progress during the most difficult portion of a nuclear project to finance (pre-construction
development costs incurred ahead of regulatory approvals or construction). The DOE award is
expected to reflect 50/50 cost sharing; i.e., the private portion is expected to also be
$400 million. Holtec will fund the private portion of these cost-shared funds. Of note, DOE’s
selection criteria included a review of the commercial viability of the project and the applicant’s
ability to obtain full financing for construction. [[


                                                                             ]]*
Palisades SMR, LLC plans to finance up to 80% of the construction cost of the Project via a
construction loan. Holtec is working on Palisades SMR, LLC’s behalf to secure a loan guarantee
from the DOE’s Office of Energy Dominance Financing (OEDF, formerly the Loan Program
Office) under Title XVII of the Energy Policy Act of 2005, as amended. Holtec has completed the
part I loan application process and is preparing to submit its part II loan application for the
Project. Part II loan applications are made after screening for part I is complete and after OEDF
requests the part II application.
Palisades SMR, LLC’s affiliate, Holtec Palisades, LLC, obtained a $1.52 billion Title XVII loan
guarantee from OEDF to support the Palisades Nuclear Plant restart project—the second such
loan guarantee issued for a nuclear project. Holtec International provided the equity contribution
for the Palisades loan. While some pre-construction work has begun on the SMR-300
construction project, the capital requirements for the Palisades restart project will not impact the
capital requirements for the SMR-300 construction. Palisades is expected to achieve
commercial operations in of 2026. Holtec also previously obtained $148 million cost-share
award through DOE’s ARDP to support development of the SMR-300 design.
In addition to the OEDF loan guarantee, Palisades SMR, LLC and Holtec are evaluating
alternative public and private construction financing, but the Title XVII loan guarantee process is
currently the expected path.
The remaining 20% equity contribution will be made up of Holtec’s private investment in the
Project accrued to the date of loan closing, additional third-party private investment, and other
sources of capital.

The Project is expected to qualify for tax credits and adders above the base credit under
Section 48E of the Internal Revenue Code. Holtec has experience with financing structures to
leverage nuclear energy tax credits and the compliance requirements associated with various
tax credit adders. Financing for the Palisades restart project is supported by similar Section 45Y

Organizational Experience and Capabilities
Holtec’s management team has extensive experience executing and financing large nuclear
projects, including prior success obtaining federal and state financial support. Several members
of Holtec’s Executive Committee members and the officers of Palisades SMR, LLC led the
development and negotiation of the Title XVII loan guarantee from OEDF for the Palisades
restart project, the parallel grant from the State of Michigan, offtake agreements with regional

including certified financial statements, to the NRC upon issuance of such reports.
